Bromeliaceae.key_door: peltate absorptive trichomes + 3 sepals + 3 petals + 6 stamens; Tillandsia epiphytic/entire/plumose-seeded vs Hechtia terrestrial-spinose/dioecious

Typhaceae.key_door: rhizomatous emergent wetland plant + upper staminate spike + lower pistillate cylinder; cautious T. domingensis vs T. latifolia character suite

taxonomy_notes: Tillandsia recurvata, Tillandsia usneoides, and Hechtia texensis remain accepted current concepts.
Hechtia texensis is accepted from southwestern Texas to northeastern Mexico; strict Hays-area treatment remains species-level.
Typha domingensis and Typha latifolia remain accepted and native to Texas.
Current Kew recognizes Typhaceae with two accepted genera, Typha and Sparganium; only Typha is in the current project pool.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Do not call Tillandsia parasitic; epiphytic support is not host parasitism.
Do not identify Typha species from gap width or leaf width alone because hybridization and plasticity can blur those characters.
